_about.what: Shoulder & rotator cuff — one move per object in "moves". The app reads this file directly: save it, reload the page. Every field name is checked, so a typo is reported with the file and move it is in.
_about.add: Copy a move that looks like the new one, paste it into "moves", give it a new id and change every field. Or: node scripts/catalog.js new <file> <id>  — writes a template with placeholder text to replace.
_about.remove: Delete the move's object (and the comma before or after it). Routines built in the app that used it will show it as missing.
_about.check: node scripts/catalog.js check  — or reload the app: a bad file shows the error on screen instead of the exercise list.
_about.names: Anything written as a word instead of an object — "metric": "knee", "template": "lean", "preset": "standing", "conditions": "balance" — is looked up in shared.json. Add reusable pieces there, not here.
_about.notes: Any field starting with "_" is a note for people and is ignored: "_note": "physio wants this re-checked".

fields.id: Unique name, used in links and saved sessions — never change it once the move has been used. Lower-case letters, digits, underscores. Good: "seated_knee_ext". Bad: "Seated Knee Ext", "knee-ext", "1_knee".
fields.name: What the user sees in the list. Good: "Seated knee extension". Bad: a clinical term nobody outside physio uses ("Open-chain terminal extension").
fields.clinicalName: Optional. The term a physio would use, shown in the details panel under the name.
fields.type: "reps" (counted) or "hold" (seconds in position). A stretch held for 30 s is a hold; ten slow raises are reps.
fields.view: "side" or "front" — where the phone stands. Side-on for anything that bends forward/back (knees, hips, spine); front-on for anything that goes out to the side (leg raise to the side, arm raise to the side, knees caving in).
fields.tracking: What the camera can honestly do: "form" (counts AND judges — needs at least one fault with a measurement and a threshold), "reps" (counts only; faults are listed for the person to watch), "none" (nothing to measure — the guide is shown and the set is logged by hand). Bad: "form" on a move whose faults are all words; the file will not load.
fields.vetted: Optional, true/false. true = a physio has recorded and checked this move in the Studio; vetted moves list first.
fields.equipment: List of words: ["none"], ["chair"], ["band", "door anchor"]. Optional extras say so: "ankle weight (optional)".
fields.muscles: { "primary": [...], "secondary": [...] } — plain names ("quadriceps", "gluteus medius"). primary must have at least one.
fields.sided: Only for one-sided moves: { "limb": "leg" | "arm" | "side", "by": "camera" | "pick", "auto": true }. "camera" = the limb nearest the phone is the working one (side-on moves); "pick" = the person chooses (front-on moves); "auto": true = when no side was chosen, watch both and follow the one that moves. Leave the field out for two-sided moves.
fields.upperBody: true when the legs need not be in frame (seated desk moves, shoulder work). Default false.
fields.summary: One line for the list. Good: "Sitting, straighten one knee until the leg is level, hold, and lower." Bad: a paragraph.
fields.setup: Where the phone goes and how to start, in the user's words. Good: "Sit tall on a chair, side-on to the phone, working leg nearest…" Bad: "Standard set-up."
fields.brief: What the coach SAYS out loud as the set begins: the position and the movement in one or two short sentences, no camera talk (the person has already placed the phone). Keep it under about 35 words — it is spoken while they get into position. Good: "Lie on your back, working leg straight. Slide the heel toward your bottom as far as it will go, then slide it back out." Bad: "Stand 2.5 m from the camera at hip height" (set-up, not movement) or a paragraph. Leave it out and the coach says only the name and the target.
fields.why: Why this camera angle can measure this move. Shown to the user; keeps the author honest. Good: "Side-on the knee angle runs from 90° to straight." Bad: left empty.
fields.calibrationPose: Optional. The still position held for the first two seconds of every set, which the coach measures against. Good: "Sitting tall, knee bent to 90°, foot hanging."
fields.camera: { "height": "floor" | "knee" | "hip" | "chest" | "eye", "distance": "2 m", "posture": "standing" | "sitting" | "lying" | "prone" | "sidelying" | "kneeling", "tolerance": 25 }. Leave it out to use the file's default at the top. posture also decides how the stick figure is pinned in place, and how a crooked phone is levelled at calibration (a standing or sitting trunk is upright, a lying one is along the floor; kneeling makes no assumption). tolerance: degrees the person may turn away from the ideal view mid-set before the coach says to turn back; leave it out for the settings.json default. Good: 20–30. Bad: 5 (nobody stands that still) or 60 (the joint is hidden by then).
fields.targets: Optional list of rep counts / hold seconds the bubble cycles through, e.g. [6, 8, 10, 12]. Leave it out for the standard choices in settings.json.
fields.defaultTarget: The one of targets selected to begin with. Must be in the list. Leave it out with targets.
fields.progress: How far through a rep the person is. { "metric": <measurement>, "start": "calibrated" | number, "target": number | "opt:rom" }. "calibrated" = whatever the measurement reads in the start position; "startMin"/"startMax" clamp it (a knee that calibrates at 150° is treated as 160°). target = the reading at a full rep, or with "targetIsDelta": true a change from the start — "delta": -1 when the reading goes DOWN during the rep (a knee angle closing). Only for type "reps" with tracking "form" or "reps". Good: knee angle from calibrated to 172. Bad: start and target the same number.
fields.hold: For type "hold" with tracking on: { "conditions": [ { "metric": <measurement>, "rel": "abs" | "change", "min": n, "max": n } ] } — the hold counts while every condition is met. "change" = relative to the calibrated start. A condition may carry "when": [{ "option": "variant", "is": "bent" }] so it only applies for that option. A named set ("balance") comes from shared.json.
fields.display: Optional. What the live readout shows: { "label": "bend", "unit": "°", "from": "start" } shows the progress measurement as a change from the start ("abs" = the raw reading); for a hold, { "condition": 0, "label": "knee", "aim": "90°" } shows that hold condition. Without it the app shows the raw progress reading.
fields.enterCue: Optional, holds only: what the coach says when the person has been out of position for a few seconds. Good: "Slide down the wall until your knees are at ninety".
fields.faults: What goes wrong, in the order they matter. Each: { "id", "label", "cue" (spoken, ≤ 8 words, what TO do), "tip" (written, why it matters), "severity" 1–3 }. Add "metric", "op" ("<" or ">"), "threshold" and the camera watches for it; leave those out and it is listed for the person to watch. "minP" (0–1) = ignore until this far into the rep; "persist" ms before it is spoken, "cooldown" ms before the same cue may repeat (rules included, so one that is true every rep is not said every rep); "rel": "change" compares to the calibrated start. "when": a list of gates that must all hold for the fault to count — { "option": "variant", "is": "bent" }, { "metric": <measurement>, "op": "<", "threshold": 168 }, "inPosition" or "notInPosition". "phase": "moving" / "rest" (reps) or "any" (a hold fault that must fire while the person is OUT of position; otherwise hold faults only watch the held position). "scale": { "metric": "progress", "times": 0.35 } makes the threshold grow with another reading. Rules instead of a measurement: "rule": "shallow" (rep did not reach the target), "fast" with "minMs", "return" with "threshold" (rep ended above this progress — did not come all the way back). Or "template": "lean" with a "threshold" to reuse one from shared.json. Good cue: "Sit tall". Bad cue: "You are leaning back again" (tells them what is wrong, not what to do).
fields.guide: { "surface": what to stand/lie on, "stop": when to stop, "cannotSee": what the person must check themselves, "regions": [ { "name": "Trunk", "points": [ { "t": "one form point", "tracked": true|false } ] } ] }. tracked: true only when a fault with a measurement actually checks that point — it is shown to the user as "camera watches".
fields.pose: The two-frame stick figure. { "A": start keyframe, "B": end keyframe, "work": { "thigh": 1, "glute": 0.5 } muscles to light up 0–1, "props": [ { "kind": "box" | "bar" | "disc" | "band", "at": "hip" } ], "wall": "behind" | "ahead", "anchor": joint(s) that stay put }. Side-view keyframe angles in degrees: torso (from vertical, + = leaning forward), thigh & shin (from hanging straight down, + = forward), foot (+ = toes up), uarm & farm (arms, + = forward), plus the far limb: thighF, shinF, footF, uarmF, farmF; face: "right" | "left". Front-view: legL, legR, shinL, shinR, armL, armR, foreL, foreR (+ = out to the side), lean, headTilt, squat 0–1. "preset": "standing" | "seated" | "supine" | "prone" | "quadruped" fills the usual values first. Check it on /figures.html.
fields.tempo: Free text. Good: "Up 2 s, hold 2 s, down 3 s."
fields.contraindications: When not to do it. Shown as "Do not do this if".
fields.sources: Optional list of { "name", "url" } added to the file's own sources.
fields.band: Optional. "none", "yellow", "red"… = offers the band-colour bubble with that default; true = offers it defaulting to none.
fields.minMs: Optional, reps only: the quickest a rep may take before "Too fast" fires (when the move lists no live fault of its own). Default in settings.json.
fields.options: Advanced: extra bubbles, e.g. a range target { "key": "rom", "label": "Range target", "values": [45, 60, 75, 90], "unit": "°", "default": 90 } referenced from progress.target as "opt:rom".
fields.figure: Advanced: point keyframes captured by the Studio instead of pose angles. Prefer pose.
fields.focus: Advanced: the landmark the live view highlights, e.g. "KNEE". Default: the last point of the progress measurement.
fields.group: Optional. The heading the move is listed under; default = the file's group at the top.
fields.region: Optional. The body region for filtering; default = the file's region.
fields.icon: Optional short label used where an icon is expected. Default "move".
fields.order: Optional. Position in the list; default = the file's order + position in this file.

sources.name: Kingston & Richmond NHS — shoulder exercises for rotator cuff tear
ACE — five essential rotator cuff exercises

moves.name: Band pull-apart
moves.summary: Arms straight at shoulder height, pull the band to your chest — checked for bending elbows, shrugging, the band drifting up or down, and short reps.
moves.setup: Hold the band in front of you at shoulder height, arms straight, hands a little wider than the shoulders, light tension. Face the camera about 2.5 m away, camera at chest height, head to hips in frame. Pull the hands apart until the band touches your chest, squeeze the shoulder blades together, pause, then return slowly.
moves.brief: Hold the band in front of you at shoulder height, arms straight, hands a little wider than the shoulders. Pull the hands apart until the band touches the chest, then return slowly.
moves.why: Facing the camera the arms open into a T in the camera plane: the distance between the hands, a bending elbow, the shoulders rising, and the hands drifting above or below shoulder height are all read directly.

guide.surface: Standing or sitting tall, facing the camera. Hold a light band in front of you at shoulder height, hands a little wider than the shoulders, palms down or thumbs up.

points.t: Feet hip-width, knees soft (or sit tall on a chair without leaning on the backrest).
Ribs down, gentle brace, back neutral — do not lean back or flare the ribs to finish the rep; that is a sign the band is too strong.
Arms straight with a tiny soft bend, held fixed. Bending the elbows turns it into a row and takes the rear shoulder out of it — the coach flags elbows bending as the band opens.
Keep the hands level with the shoulders the whole way. As you tire the band drifts down toward the stomach; the coach flags hands more than a hand-width above or below shoulder height.
Pull until the band touches the chest with the arms out in a T, pause, then return under control.
Wrists straight; thumbs up (palms facing each other) is the gentlest variation for irritable shoulders.
Start the rep by sliding the shoulder blades back, then let the hands follow. Squeeze the blades together at the end without shrugging.
Shoulders down and away from the ears; long neck, wide collarbones. A rising shoulder is flagged.
Chin level, eyes on the camera; do not crane the neck forward.
Breathe out as the band opens, in as it closes.
1–2 s apart, 1 s squeeze, 3 s back together.

guide.stop: Pinching at the front of the shoulder, neck pain, or numbness in the hands — switch to a lighter band or a wider grip before stopping altogether.

moves.tempo: 1–2 s apart, 1 s squeeze, 3 s back.
moves.progression: Next band colour; hands closer together.
moves.contraindications: Pain at the front of the shoulder as the band opens.

faults.label: Elbows bending
faults.cue: Arms long — pull with the shoulder blades
faults.tip: Bending the elbows turns the pull-apart into a row and takes the rear shoulder out of it. Keep a tiny soft bend and hold it fixed.

faults.label: Shrugging
faults.tip: Pull the shoulders gently down before each rep: wide collarbones, then squeeze the blades back. If they climb toward the ears the upper trapezius takes over.

faults.label: Hands dropping below shoulder height
faults.cue: Keep the band at shoulder height
faults.tip: As you tire the band drifts down toward the stomach and the movement becomes a shoulder extension. Keep the hands level with the shoulders the whole way.

faults.label: Hands rising above shoulder height
faults.cue: Bring the band down to shoulder height
faults.tip: Pulling above the shoulders loads the neck. Hands level with the shoulders.

faults.label: Not pulling all the way apart
faults.cue: All the way — band to the chest
faults.tip: Finish with the band touching the chest and a one-second squeeze. If that is not possible, use a lighter band.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: One to two seconds apart, a one-second squeeze, three seconds back. Do not let the band snap the arms together.

moves.name: Band rows
moves.summary: Pull the band to your ribs with the elbows close — checked for shrugging, leaning back, flaring elbows and incomplete pulls.
moves.setup: Anchor the band at waist height in front of you. Stand side-on to the camera about 2.5 m away, camera at chest height, whole body in frame. Arms straight toward the anchor with light tension. Draw the elbows straight back past your ribs, squeeze the shoulder blades together, pause, and let the arms straighten slowly.
moves.brief: Anchor the band at waist height in front of you, arms straight with light tension. Pull the elbows back to the ribs, squeeze the shoulder blades, then return slowly.
moves.why: From the side the elbow travelling behind the line of the torso, the shoulder rising, and the trunk leaning back are all plain to see; from the front they are hidden behind the body.

guide.surface: Standing side-on to the camera, band anchored at waist height in front of you (door anchor at handle height, railing, pole). Step back until there is light tension with the arms straight.

points.t: Feet hip-width, one foot slightly ahead if that feels steadier, knees soft. Slight hinge at the hips is fine; the trunk then stays at that angle for every rep.
Brace like a standing plank: ribs down, abdomen firm, back neutral. The body does not rock back to help the pull — the coach compares your trunk angle to the start position.
If you feel yourself leaning back or the lower back arching, the band is too strong.
Start with the arms long and the shoulder blades allowed to glide forward. Then draw the elbows straight back past the ribs, keeping them close to the body — not flared out to shoulder height.
Elbows lead; the hands follow. Finish with the hands beside the lower ribs and the elbows behind the line of the torso.
Wrists straight, grip relaxed — do not curl the band in with the biceps.
Let the arms straighten fully on the way out so every rep goes through the whole range.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together and DOWN at the back of each rep. If the shoulders rise toward the ears the upper trapezius is doing the row — the coach flags it.
Chin level, neck long; do not poke the head forward as you pull.
Breathe out as you pull, in as the arms lengthen.
2 s back, 1–2 s squeeze, 3 s forward under control. Never let the band snap the arms out.

guide.stop: Sharp pain at the front of the shoulder, neck pain that builds through the set, or pins and needles in the hands.

moves.tempo: 2 s back, 1 s squeeze, 3 s forward.
moves.contraindications: Neck or shoulder pain during the pull.

faults.label: Shrugging
faults.tip: Pull the shoulder blades down and back, not up. If the shoulder rises toward the ear the upper trapezius is doing the row.

faults.label: Leaning back
faults.cue: Stand tall — pull with the arms
faults.tip: Rocking the torso back uses body weight instead of the back muscles. Brace the abdomen and keep the trunk still; if you must lean, the band is too strong.

faults.label: Elbows flaring up
faults.cue: Elbows down, close to your ribs
faults.tip: Elbows at shoulder height turn this into a high row that loads the neck. Keep the elbows low and brushing your sides.

faults.label: Not pulling all the way back
faults.cue: Elbows further back — squeeze the blades
faults.tip: The squeeze at the end is the point of the exercise: the elbow should pass behind your ribs before you pause.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Two seconds back, hold the squeeze for a count, three seconds forward. Do not let the band snap the arms out.

faults.label: Not letting the arms straighten
faults.cue: Let the arms reach forward fully
faults.tip: Each rep starts with the arms long so the shoulder blades can glide forward and then be pulled back through the full range.

moves.name: Shoulder abduction (band)
moves.summary: Straight-arm raise out to the side against a band, to shoulder height — checked for shrugging, leaning, bending the elbow and swinging too high.
moves.setup: Stand on the band, hold the other end at your side. Face the camera about 2.5 m away, camera at chest height, whole body in frame. Raise the arm straight out to the side, thumb slightly up, no higher than shoulder level, then lower slowly.
moves.brief: Stand on the band, hold the other end at your side. Raise the arm straight out to the side, thumb slightly up, no higher than shoulder level, then lower slowly.
moves.why: From the front the arm swings across the camera plane, so the raise angle, a bending elbow, a rising shoulder and a trunk leaning the other way are all measured directly — the same geometry that makes standing hip abduction easy to track.

guide.surface: Standing on the middle of the band with the foot on the working side (or both feet), holding the other end at your thigh. Firm floor, shoes on so the band cannot slip.

points.t: Feet hip-width, knees soft, weight even. The band runs from under the foot straight up to the hand.
Stand tall with the trunk still. Leaning the body away from the arm makes the arm look higher without the shoulder working — the coach measures trunk lean against your start position.
Ribs down, no arching. If you have to lean or swing, the band is too strong.
Arm straight with a soft elbow — set the tiny bend before the first rep and keep it fixed. A bending elbow is flagged.
Raise straight out to the side, slightly in front of the body line (about 30° forward — the "scapular plane"), thumb pointing slightly up. Palm down with the thumb dropped is harder on the joint.
Stop at shoulder height (hand level with the shoulder, 90°). Higher than that the shoulder blade has to rotate and the joint is more easily pinched; the coach flags raises past ~100°.
Lead with the elbow, not the hand; think of pushing the hand toward the far wall rather than lifting it.
Shoulder blade set down and back before each rep; the shoulder must not rise toward the ear as the arm goes up. This is the fault the coach watches most closely.
Neck long, chin level, eyes forward.
Hanging relaxed or hand on hip. Do not hold a chair on that side — it invites leaning.
Breathe out on the way up, in on the way down.
2 s up, 1 s pause at the top, 3 s down. No swinging — every rep starts from a dead stop.

guide.stop: A sharp catch or "painful arc" partway up, pain on top of the shoulder that lingers after the set, or any pins and needles in the hand.

moves.tempo: 2 s up, 1 s pause, 3 s down.
moves.progression: Next band colour; thumb-up raise to 90°.
moves.contraindications: Pain in the arc between 60° and 120°, or a recent shoulder dislocation.

faults.label: Shrugging
faults.tip: If the shoulder rises toward the ear the upper trapezius does the lift. Set the shoulder blade down first; think of reaching the hand toward the wall rather than lifting it.

faults.label: Leaning away
faults.tip: Tipping the trunk the other way makes the arm look higher without the shoulder working. Keep the torso upright and accept a smaller raise.

faults.label: Elbow bending
faults.cue: Keep the arm straight — soft elbow
faults.tip: A bending elbow shortens the lever and shifts work to the biceps. Keep a small soft bend and hold it fixed for the whole rep.

faults.label: Raising above shoulder height
faults.tip: The tender range for most irritable shoulders is roughly 60–120°, so rehab usually stops with the hand level with the shoulder. Go higher later, once it is comfortable.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Aim for the raise target without shrugging or leaning; if it hurts before then, lower the target.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.cue: Slower — two up, pause, three down
faults.tip: Swinging the arm lets momentum lift it. Two seconds up, a one-second pause at the top, three seconds down.

moves.name: Standing shoulder rotation (band)
moves.summary: External or internal rotation with the elbow pinned to your side — the classic rotator-cuff exercise, checked for elbow drift, shrugging and trunk twist.
moves.setup: Anchor the band at elbow height beside you (door handle, railing). Stand facing the camera about 2 m away, camera at chest height, head to hips in frame. Elbow bent to 90° and touching your ribs, forearm across your stomach for external rotation (or out to the side for internal rotation). Rotate the forearm against the band, elbow glued to your side, then return slowly.
moves.brief: Anchor the band at elbow height beside you. Elbow bent to 90 degrees and pinned to the ribs, rotate the forearm outward, then return slowly.
moves.why: Facing the camera, the forearm swings across the picture like a clock hand, so rotation angle is read directly, and the elbow leaving the ribs, the shoulder rising toward the ear and the torso twisting are all visible as changes the camera can measure.

guide.surface: Standing, on a firm floor. Band anchored at elbow height — a door anchor, a railing or a heavy table leg — beside you on the side away from the working arm (external rotation) or on the same side (internal rotation). Light band to start.

points.t: Feet hip-width apart, weight even, knees soft. Stand tall; do not brace against the band by leaning.
Chest square to the camera for the whole set. The most common cheat is turning the torso to add range: the shoulders narrow in the picture and the coach flags it.
Ribs down, gentle abdominal brace. No arching the lower back.
Elbow bent to 90° and touching your ribs for the whole rep. A folded towel between elbow and ribs is the classic cue — if it drops, the elbow has drifted.
External rotation: start with the hand in front of the stomach and rotate the forearm outward like a gate opening; internal rotation: start out to the side and bring the hand to the stomach.
Wrist straight and firm, in line with the forearm; the band pulls on the hand, not the wrist.
Rotate to the target angle (45–90°) without the elbow moving; stop where it is comfortable, never into a pinch.
Both shoulders down and level, away from the ears. The shoulder blade sits back and down before the first rep.
Neck long, jaw relaxed, eyes on the camera.
Relaxed at your side or resting on your hip. It should not steady the band.
Breathe out as you rotate against the band, in as you return.
2 s out, brief pause, 3 s back. The slow return is where the rotator cuff works hardest.

guide.stop: Sharp or pinching pain in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling down the arm, or pain that does not settle within a few minutes of stopping.

moves.tempo: 2 s out, brief pause, 3 s back.
moves.progression: Next band colour; a pause at the end of range.
moves.regression: Lighter band or no band; smaller range.
moves.contraindications: Sharp shoulder pain, or pain that lingers after the set.

faults.label: Elbow leaving your side
faults.tip: Once the elbow lifts away from the body the movement becomes a shoulder swing and the rotator cuff stops doing the work. Tuck a folded towel between elbow and ribs and keep it pinned.

faults.label: Elbow opening past 90°
faults.cue: Keep the elbow bent at ninety
faults.tip: If the elbow straightens the hand swings down and the movement stops being rotation. Forearm level with the floor, elbow at a right angle, for the whole rep.

faults.label: Twisting the torso
faults.cue: Chest to the camera — arm only
faults.tip: Turning the trunk fakes extra range. Keep both shoulders square to the camera and accept less rotation.

faults.label: Shrugging
faults.cue: Shoulder down, away from your ear
faults.tip: When the shoulder creeps up the upper trapezius takes over. Set the shoulder blade down and back before each rep and keep the neck long.

faults.label: Elbow bent past 90°
faults.cue: Forearm level — open the elbow to ninety
faults.tip: Pulling the hand up toward the chest shortens the lever and shifts the work to the biceps. Keep the forearm parallel to the floor.

faults.label: Leaning
faults.tip: Leaning sideways or back recruits the trunk. Feet hip-width, ribs down, stay upright.

faults.label: Not reaching the rotation target
faults.tip: Take the forearm through the full comfortable range each rep; if it is not reachable, lower the target rather than cheat with the elbow.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.cue: Slower — two seconds out, three back
faults.tip: The return against the band is where the cuff works hardest. Two seconds out, brief pause, three seconds back.

faults.label: Not returning fully
faults.cue: All the way back to the start
faults.tip: Finish each rep back at the start position so the muscle works through its whole range.

moves.name: Pendulum
equipment: table or chair to lean on
moves.summary: Bent over with the arm hanging, let it swing in small circles using the body, not the shoulder muscles.
moves.setup: Lean forward with the good hand on a table, let the affected arm hang straight down. Rock the body so the arm swings forward and back, then in small circles, growing the circle only as pain allows.
moves.why: The arm swings in circles toward and away from the phone, with no rep to count. This is a mobility drill for the early days: follow the guide and log the time.
moves.dosage: 1–2 minutes, a few times a day.
moves.progression: Larger circles; a light weight in the hand for traction.

faults.label: Swinging with the shoulder muscles
faults.tip: The body rocks and the arm follows like a rope; if the shoulder is working, it is not a pendulum.

faults.label: Circles too big too soon
faults.tip: Dinner-plate size to start; grow it over days, not minutes.

faults.label: Elbow bent
faults.tip: A bent elbow means the shoulder is holding on. The arm should hang like a rope from the socket.

faults.label: Rounding the back to lean
faults.tip: Support yourself on a table and fold at the hips; rounding the back loads it for nothing.

guide.surface: A stable table to lean on.
guide.stop: Pain that grows during the swings.
guide.cannotSee: Whether the shoulder is relaxed or working.

points.t: Hangs loose; movement comes from the trunk rocking.
Bent forward, other hand supporting on the table.

moves.name: Wall slide
moves.summary: Back and arms against a wall in a goalpost shape, slide the arms up overhead and back down.
moves.setup: Stand with your back on a wall, feet a little forward, ribs down. Bend the elbows to 90° with the backs of the wrists and elbows touching the wall. Slide the arms up as far as they go without the wrists leaving the wall, then down.
moves.brief: Stand with your back on a wall, feet a little forward, ribs down. Bend the elbows to 90° with the backs of the wrists and elbows touching the wall.
moves.why: Facing the phone, the arms rise in the camera plane, so their angle counts the reps, and the shoulder hiking toward the ear shows as the ear–shoulder distance shrinking.
moves.progression: Slide higher; add a light band around the wrists.
moves.regression: Stop where the wrists start to leave the wall.
moves.contraindications: Pinching at the top of the shoulder.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Wrists leaving the wall
faults.cue: Keep the wrists on the wall
faults.tip: Go only as high as the wrists can stay in contact; the range grows over weeks.

faults.label: Arching the back to go higher
faults.tip: When the range runs out the back arches to fake it. Stop where the ribs stay down.

faults.label: Not pressing into the wall
faults.tip: Light pressure into the wall the whole way is what switches on the shoulder blade muscles.

guide.surface: A flat wall, no skirting to catch the heels.
guide.stop: Pinching or sharp pain at the top of the shoulder.
guide.cannotSee: The wrists and elbows losing contact with the wall.

points.t: Stay down as the arms rise.
Backs of the wrists and elbows on the wall throughout.
Ribs down, lower back close to the wall.

moves.name: Scaption
moves.summary: Raise a straight arm to shoulder height about 30° in front of the side, thumb up.
moves.setup: Face the phone with a light weight, thumb pointing up. Raise the arm in the plane of the shoulder blade — a little in front of straight out to the side — to shoulder height, then lower slowly.
moves.brief: Stand with a light weight, thumb pointing up. Raise the arm in the plane of the shoulder blade to shoulder height, then lower slowly.
moves.why: The upper arm rises in the camera plane, so its angle counts the reps; the shoulder hiking is the fault to watch and shows as the ear–shoulder gap closing.
moves.progression: Heavier weight; both arms at once.
moves.contraindications: Pain in the painful arc (60–120°) that does not settle.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Arm drifting straight out or forward
faults.tip: Scaption is the 30–45° plane. Straight out to the side is a different, tighter exercise.

faults.label: Thumb pointing down
faults.tip: Thumb down closes the space at the top of the shoulder. Lead with the thumb up.

faults.label: Going above shoulder height
faults.tip: The cuff works best up to horizontal; higher just adds strain.

faults.label: Dropping the arm
faults.tip: Lowering slowly is where a cuff tendon is loaded most usefully.

guide.cannotSee: Whether the arm is truly in the shoulder-blade plane.

points.t: Straight, thumb up, 30° forward of the side, to shoulder height.
Stays down and back; no hiking.

moves.name: Y-T-W raises
moves.summary: Face down, lift the arms into a Y, then a T, then a W, squeezing the shoulder blades each time.
moves.setup: Lie on your front or hinge forward, arms hanging. Lift the arms to make a Y (thumbs up, overhead), lower; a T (straight out), lower; a W (elbows bent, squeezed down and back), lower. That is one round.
moves.why: Three different arm positions in one set, mostly moving toward or away from the phone when face down. Nothing here counts cleanly; follow the guide and log the rounds.
moves.tempo: Lift 2 s, hold 2 s, lower 2 s, each letter.
moves.progression: Light dumbbells; on an incline bench.

faults.label: Shrugging into the ears
faults.tip: Each letter starts by pulling the shoulder blades down; the arms follow.

faults.label: Lifting the head and neck
faults.tip: Keep the forehead on the floor or a towel; the arms lift, not the head.

faults.label: Lifting too high
faults.cue: Just off the floor is enough
faults.tip: A couple of centimetres with the blades squeezed beats a big lift from the lower back.

faults.label: Rushing between letters
faults.tip: Y, T and W each need the blades set again. Run them together and the traps take over.

guide.cannotSee: The shoulder blades — the movement is under the body from the phone’s angle.

points.t: Squeeze down and back before each lift.
Nose down, neck long.

moves.name: Push-up plus
moves.summary: At the top of a push-up (or on the knees), push the floor away further so the shoulder blades spread apart.
moves.setup: Hands under the shoulders, on the knees or toes, side-on to the phone. With the elbows locked, push the floor away so the upper back rounds slightly and the shoulder blades slide apart; then let them come together. That is the plus.
moves.brief: Hands under the shoulders, on the knees or toes. With the elbows locked, push the floor away so the upper back rounds slightly and the shoulder blades slide apart, then let them come together.
moves.why: From the side the shoulder rises a few centimetres away from the hand at the top of each plus, which the phone can count. It is a small movement, so only the count is trusted.
moves.progression: From the toes; feet on a step.
moves.regression: Hands on a wall (wall push-up plus).

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Skipping the push at the top
faults.cue: Push the floor away at the top
faults.tip: The extra push that rounds the upper back is the whole exercise; a normal push-up misses it.

faults.label: Bending the elbows
faults.tip: The plus is at the shoulder blades, not the elbows; keep the arms straight.

faults.label: Hips sagging
faults.tip: Brace the stomach so the body stays one line from head to knees.

faults.label: Shrugging instead of protracting
faults.tip: The blades slide apart around the ribs — they should not travel up toward the ears.

guide.surface: Mat under the knees or hands.
guide.cannotSee: The shoulder blades spreading — it reads the shoulder lifting as a proxy.

points.t: Push the floor away until the blades spread; elbows locked.
Straight from head to knees.

moves.name: Sleeper stretch
moves.summary: Lying on the affected side, elbow at 90°, gently press the forearm down toward the floor.
moves.setup: Lie on the affected side, rolled very slightly back so you are on the outer edge of the shoulder blade — that pins it and is what keeps the stretch safe. Shoulder and elbow at 90°, forearm pointing up. With the other hand, press the forearm gently toward the floor until a stretch is felt behind the shoulder. Hold. Stop short of pinching.
moves.why: The rotation happens toward the phone whichever way it is placed, and the pressure is applied by hand. Follow the guide and log the hold.
moves.tempo: Ease in over 5 s, hold, release.
moves.progression: Roll slightly forward (the modified version) if the front pinches.
moves.contraindications: Pinching at the front of the shoulder — this stretch is not for everyone; a mild stretch behind the shoulder is the only target.

faults.label: Forcing the forearm down
faults.tip: A mild stretch behind the shoulder; pressing hard makes the joint guard.

faults.label: Shoulder blade not pinned
faults.tip: Lie slightly back onto the outer edge of the shoulder blade so it cannot slide. Without that the stretch pinches the front.

faults.label: Feeling it at the front
faults.tip: The stretch belongs behind the shoulder. Pinching at the front means stop and ask your physio.

faults.label: Rolling onto the back
faults.tip: Keep the shoulder blade pinned so the stretch stays in the capsule.

guide.surface: Firm floor with a pillow under the head.
guide.stop: Pinching at the front, or pain that lingers afterwards.
guide.cannotSee: The rotation and the hand pressure.

points.t: Directly under you, elbow bent 90°, forearm pressed gently toward the floor.

moves.name: Wall angel
moves.summary: Back flat on a wall, arms in a W, sweep them up to a Y and back keeping every part in contact.
moves.setup: Stand with the head, upper back and tailbone on a wall, feet a step out. Arms in a W with the backs of the hands and elbows on the wall. Slide up toward a Y and back down without anything leaving the wall.
moves.brief: Stand with the head, upper back and tailbone on a wall, feet a step out. Arms in a W with the backs of the hands and elbows on the wall.
moves.why: The arms sweep in the camera plane, so their angle counts the reps, and the shoulders hiking toward the ears is visible as the ear–shoulder gap shrinking.
moves.progression: Slide the feet closer to the wall.
moves.regression: Halve the range and keep every contact point.
moves.contraindications: Lower back pain from arching to keep contact.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Arms peeling off the wall
faults.tip: Cut the range in half and keep hands, wrists and elbows on the wall the whole way.

faults.label: Going higher than the contact allows
faults.tip: Your range is where the wrists, elbows and back all still touch. Going past it trains the wrong thing.

faults.label: Chin poking forward
faults.cue: Back of the head on the wall
faults.tip: The head is part of the contact. If it lifts off, the neck is compensating.

guide.stop: Shoulder pinching or lower back pain.
guide.cannotSee: The hands and elbows losing contact.

points.t: Head, upper back, tailbone, elbows and backs of hands all on the wall.
Down, not shrugged.

moves.name: Doorway pec stretch
moves.summary: Forearms on either side of a doorway, step through until the chest stretches.
moves.setup: Stand in a doorway with each forearm on the frame, elbows a little below shoulder height. Step one foot through and lean gently until the chest stretches. Hold, breathing.
moves.why: A doorway hides half the body and the lean is toward the phone; nothing measurable from one angle. Follow the guide and log the hold.
moves.tempo: Ease in over 5 s, hold, ease out.
moves.progression: Elbows higher for the lower chest fibres.
moves.regression: Less lean; one arm at a time.
moves.contraindications: Pain at the front of the shoulder.

faults.label: Shoulders rising
faults.tip: Keep the shoulder blades down and back; the stretch is in the chest, not the neck.

faults.label: Arching the lower back
faults.tip: Brace lightly and lean from the ankles, not the lower back.

faults.label: Elbow too high
faults.tip: Above shoulder height the stretch moves into the front of the joint instead of the chest.

faults.label: Leaning instead of stepping
faults.tip: Take a small step forward rather than throwing the body at the doorway.

guide.surface: A doorway you can lean into safely.
guide.stop: Front-of-shoulder pain or tingling in the hands.
guide.cannotSee: Any of it — the frame hides the arms.

points.t: Forearms on the frame, elbows just below shoulder height.
Lean from the ankles, ribs down, shoulders back.

moves.name: Band face pull
moves.summary: Pull a band toward the face with the elbows high and the hands finishing beside the ears.
moves.setup: Anchor a band at face height in front of you, hold an end in each hand, face the phone. Pull the band toward the face, elbows high and wide, hands ending beside the ears, squeezing the shoulder blades. Return slowly.
moves.brief: Anchor a band at face height in front of you, an end in each hand. Pull it toward the face, elbows high and wide, hands ending beside the ears, then return.
moves.why: Facing the phone the hands travel apart as they come back, so the wrist-to-wrist distance counts the reps. Elbow height and the squeeze itself are listed for you to check.
moves.tempo: Pull 1–2 s, squeeze 1 s, return 2 s.
moves.contraindications: Pinching at the top of the shoulder with the elbows high.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Elbows dropping low
faults.tip: The elbows stay at shoulder height or above; dropping them turns it into a row.

faults.label: Leaning back to pull
faults.tip: The band moves; the trunk does not. Stagger the feet if you need balance.

faults.label: Pulling to the chest
faults.tip: A face pull finishes at eye level with the hands wide. To the chest it is just a row.

faults.label: No external rotation at the end
faults.tip: Finish with the backs of the hands travelling back — that is the rotator cuff part.

guide.cannotSee: The shoulder blades squeezing — it reads the hands spreading as a proxy.

points.t: Elbows high and wide; hands finish beside the ears.
Upright and still.

moves.name: Shoulder flexion (lying, with a stick)
moves.summary: On your back holding a stick, let the good arm lift both arms overhead toward the floor behind you.
moves.setup: Lie on your back, side-on to the phone at floor level, holding a stick with both hands, arms pointing at the ceiling. Using the good arm to help, take the stick overhead toward the floor behind your head as far as comfortable, then back.
moves.brief: Lie on your back holding a stick in both hands, arms pointing at the ceiling. Using the good arm to help, take the stick overhead toward the floor, then back.
moves.why: From the side the arm sweeps from pointing up to overhead, so its angle counts the reps. The back arching to add range is hard to see, so it is listed.
moves.tempo: Over 3 s, hold 2 s, back 3 s.
moves.progression: Less help from the good arm; add a light weight later.
moves.contraindications: Sharp pain at the front of the shoulder near the end of range.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Arching the back to go further
faults.tip: Keep the lower back on the floor; the range should come from the shoulder.

faults.label: Forcing with the good arm
faults.tip: The good arm guides; it should not drag the sore one past the stretch.

faults.label: Shrugging at the top
faults.tip: When the range runs out the shoulder rides up. Stop just before that point.

guide.stop: Sharp pain at the end of range.

points.t: Both hands on the stick; straight as it goes overhead.
Lower back on the floor, knees bent.

moves.name: Cross-body stretch
moves.summary: Pull one straight arm across the chest with the other hand until the back of the shoulder stretches.
moves.setup: Face the phone, bring the working arm across the chest at shoulder height and hug it in with the other forearm. Keep the shoulder down. Hold.
moves.brief: Bring the working arm across the chest at shoulder height and hug it in with the other forearm. Keep that shoulder down and hold.
moves.why: The hand held near the opposite shoulder is visible from the front, so the timer runs while the arm is actually across the body.
moves.tempo: Ease in over 5 s, hold, release.
moves.progression: Pull slightly lower across the chest.
moves.contraindications: Pinching at the front of the shoulder.

faults.label: Shoulder rising
faults.tip: Keep the working shoulder down and back; the stretch belongs behind it.

faults.label: Pulling on the elbow
faults.tip: Hooking the elbow twists the joint; hold above the elbow and draw the arm across.

faults.label: Turning the trunk
faults.tip: The trunk stays square to the phone; only the arm moves.

faults.label: Shoulder riding up
faults.tip: The stretched shoulder must stay down or the stretch goes into the neck.

points.t: Straight, across the chest at shoulder height, hugged in.
Down and back.

moves.name: External rotation (side-lying)
moves.summary: Lying on your side, elbow tucked with a towel, rotate a light weight up toward the ceiling.
moves.setup: Lie on your side facing the phone (on the floor, 1.5 m away), top elbow bent to 90° and pinned to the waist over a rolled towel, forearm across the stomach. Rotate the hand up toward the ceiling, pause, lower slowly.
moves.brief: Lie on your side, top elbow bent to 90 degrees and pinned to the waist, forearm across the stomach. Rotate the hand up toward the ceiling, pause, then lower slowly.
moves.why: The forearm swings up in the camera plane, so its angle counts each rep. Whether the elbow stays pinned is listed for you to feel.
moves.tempo: Up 2 s, hold 1 s, down 3 s.
moves.contraindications: Shoulder pain that builds through the set.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Elbow lifting off the waist
faults.cue: Keep the elbow on the towel
faults.tip: If the elbow lifts, the deltoid takes over; keep it pressed onto the towel.

faults.label: Rolling backward
faults.tip: Keep the hips stacked; rolling back fakes the range.

faults.label: Rolling the trunk back
faults.tip: Rolling backwards fakes extra range. The shoulder rotates; the body does not.

faults.label: Rotating past vertical
faults.tip: The forearm rises to upright and no further; past that gravity stops resisting anyway.

guide.surface: Firm floor, towel under the elbow.
guide.cannotSee: The elbow lifting away from the waist.

points.t: Elbow pinned at 90°; forearm rotates up toward the ceiling.
Hips and shoulders stacked.

moves.name: Shoulder shrug
moves.summary: Holding weights at the sides, lift the shoulders straight up toward the ears and lower slowly.
moves.setup: Face the phone with a weight in each hand, arms straight. Lift the shoulders straight up, pause, lower fully.
moves.brief: Stand with a weight in each hand, arms straight. Lift the shoulders straight up, pause, then lower fully.
moves.why: Facing the phone the shoulders rise toward the ears, so the ear–shoulder distance shrinking counts each rep.
moves.tempo: Up 1 s, hold 1 s, down 2 s.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Rolling the shoulders
faults.tip: Rolling adds nothing and grinds the joint; lift straight up.

faults.label: Rolling the shoulders
faults.tip: Rolling grinds the shoulder blade. Lift straight up toward the ears and lower under control.

faults.label: Jutting the chin
faults.tip: Keep the neck long and the eyes level.

faults.label: No pause at the top
faults.cue: Squeeze one second at the top
faults.tip: A brief hold at the top is where the muscle actually shortens under load.

guide.cannotSee: The shoulders rolling forward or back.

points.t: Lift straight toward the ears; lower fully.
Long, chin in.
